c.st: Ask HN: Is "The Art of Computer Programming" worth investing in?
c.x:
> I usually recommend people read "Algorithms" by Sedgewick instead.

I mean, they’re not really comparable. One will teach you computer science and algorithms. The other will tell you about Bernoulli numbers and the Gamma function, with a historical aside about the solution to the cubic equation, and then show you a neat trick for encoding some linked list manipulation in a handful of instructions on a fantasy CPU.

c.st: Ask HN: Is "The Art of Computer Programming" worth investing in?
c.x: Just skim it and read a section or two to see for yourself. It's been more than a decade since I read any of it, but IIRC it's a from-first-principles build up of theoretical computer science. Basic algorithms, stuff like that. It is foundational, but it is also common knowledge and covered in tons of other very good textbooks. I usually recommend people read "Algorithms" by Sedgewick instead.
